This is a mini Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) project that is part of the [Carnegie Mellon Sports Analytics Camp (CMSACamp) 2026](https://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/statistics-datascience/engagement/summer/cmsa-camp.html) research program.

For this project, my team was assigned a dataset of throw-level data in 4 seasons of the [Ultimate Frisbee Association (UFA)](https://watchufa.com/), formerly known as the American Ultimate Disc League (AUDL), a professional ultimate frisbee tournament. For about 2 weeks, we were tasked with exploring the dataset using programming and statistical techniques, such as data cleaning, data visualization, and clustering analysis.

In the group, I visualized the location of goals scored and turnovers made by the New York Empire, an "elite" team and the Tampa Bay Cannons, a "struggling" team, using heat maps. Both the Empire and the Cannons have approximately similar scoring patterns, but the Cannons' turnover locations are more concentrated than the Empire. This case study gives a potential reason why in ultimate frisbee, similar strategies may lead to very different outcomes depending on the team.

Throughout the project, we have learned to navigate data from a niche sport like ultimate frisbee without prior domain knowledge, familiarize ourselves with R programming and collaboration via GitHub, as well as practicing our presentation to prepare for the capstone project in CMSACamp.
